known_latex_defects_note: Pre-existing source corruption (\raisebox, stray braces/ampersands, \theta inside \text, and 4 formulas where \$ is ambiguous between literal currency and a mangled separator). Deliberately NOT auto-repaired: guessing would silently drop equations. These render as visible source under throwOnError:false rather than breaking the page.

dollar_invariant.invariant: no UNESCAPED $ in a result field. A backslash-escaped \$ is a literal currency symbol and is valid KaTeX, so a plain substring check for "$" over-reports.
dollar_invariant.note: Backend counted 6 formulas containing a $. 4 carry an UNESCAPED $ and are listed in known_latex_defects as invariant violations (ambiguous \$: currency vs mangled separator — deliberately not guessed). The other 2 are pure currency (\$3.98 - \$6.02) and render correctly; they are NOT violations.

unicode_normalization.method: runs of unicode super/subscripts collapse into a single ^{..}/_{..} group; per-character replacement produced invalid double subscripts for vulgar fractions like ¹/₁₃
unicode_normalization.measured_not_assumed: every distinct non-ASCII char in the bank was rendered through KaTeX 0.18.5; μ θ π α β ✓ × ÷ ° ≈ − → render cleanly and are left alone
unicode_normalization.mode_dependency: KaTeX unicode support is MODE-DEPENDENT: Greek letters and check marks render cleanly in math mode but have NO glyph in the text fonts, so they misrender only inside \text{...}. Verified by rendering each char in both modes. Repair is to SPLIT the text group leaving the char in math mode — substituting a command is wrong, \mu inside \text{} throws.
unicode_normalization.verified: 0 of 6,404 formulas emit a no-character-metrics warning in either mode

key_semantics.warning: template_id is NOT unique across Neo4j labels. All 791 :SolveAlong nodes share their template_id with a distinct :Problem node (verified 2026-09-03), so a label-agnostic MATCH on template_id can resolve to the wrong node.
key_semantics.rule: Always qualify the label when joining on template_id. :Problem and :SolveAlong are separate nodes and are never dual-labeled, so an id-keyed write to one does NOT touch the other.
key_semantics.this_artifact: bank `id` is the recovered template_id of SolveAlong-shaped teaching content. 766 of the 823 also name a :Problem node; 20 of the 38 quarantined ids name both labels.
key_semantics.consequence: Backend's trust import keys on these ids — it must exclude on BOTH labels if it ever serves the walkthrough pool, since excluding the :Problem alone leaves the same-id :SolveAlong untouched.
